title: Paid campaign that brings clicks but almost no sales
pass: No paid campaign with real session volume converts near zero in GA4 over the last 28 days.
fails: A paid campaign brings many sessions with almost no purchases; GA4 names the campaign and the landing page it sends people to.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-07: run_report 28 days, dimensions=[sessionCampaignName, sessionDefaultChannelGroup, landingPage], metrics=[sessions, transactions], paid channel groups only; rank by sessions and flag campaigns with real volume and near-zero transactions.
action: Check that campaign's landing page against the ad promise. Point the campaign to a page that sells, or pause it while the developer fixes the page.
done_when: The campaign is paused or points to a new landing page, and its GA4 conversion rate is up over the next 14 days.
why_it_matters: Paid clicks on this campaign are likely lost after landing, so CAC is higher than it needs to be; fixing the page or the destination is expected to raise ROAS on the same spend.
selected_because: Answers 'ads or site?' directly with a named campaign and landing page from the store's own GA4.

title: GA4 records more purchases than real orders
pass: purchase event count equals transactions, and no transaction ID appears on more than one purchase event.
fails: purchase fires more than once per order (thank-you page refresh, platform app plus GTM, two tags), so GA4 shows more purchases than real orders.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days eventName=purchase metrics=[eventCount, transactions]; second run_report dimensions=[transactionId] metrics=[eventCount], count IDs with eventCount above 1 and purchases with transactionId (not set).
action: Forward to the developer: fire purchase once per order with a unique transaction_id, and block repeats when the thank-you page is refreshed or reopened.
done_when: purchase event count equals transactions over 7 days and no transaction ID repeats.
why_it_matters: Duplicate purchases make reported ROAS read higher than real, so losing campaigns can look like winners; fixing it may lower reported ROAS, which is the truth showing, not performance dropping.
selected_because: Over-count is the top 'is the number real?' failure; this is the effect seen in GA4 order data, while the GTM list checks the Purchase tag setup that causes it.

title: GA4 purchase revenue zero, in mixed currencies, or not matching its items
pass: Every purchase in GA4 carries a numeric value and the store currency, and item revenue adds up to purchase revenue apart from shipping and tax.
fails: GA4 purchase revenue is zero or missing, more than one currency shows on purchases, or item revenue does not add up to purchase revenue (missing or duplicated items, value sent as text).
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days eventName=purchase metrics=[eventCount, purchaseRevenue, itemRevenue]; run_report dimensions=[currencyCode] for purchase; flag zero revenue, more than one currency, or item revenue far from purchase revenue.
action: Forward to the developer: the purchase event must send value as a number, the store currency, and the full items list.
done_when: purchaseRevenue is above zero, one currency shows on purchases, and item revenue matches purchase revenue apart from shipping and tax.
why_it_matters: Missing or wrong values make reported ROAS read lower than real, so value-based bidding learns from bad numbers and winning campaigns can get cut.
selected_because: Value and currency are what ROAS is built on; this reads the purchases GA4 actually stored, which the store visit cannot see because it stops at the cart.

title: Where paid visitors drop after the click
pass: For paid sessions, each step (view_item to add_to_cart, add_to_cart to begin_checkout, begin_checkout to purchase) is at or above the tool's step benchmark.
fails: One step loses most paid visitors; the worst step is named with the page behind it.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days dimensions=[eventName, sessionDefaultChannelGroup] metrics=[totalUsers] for view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, purchase, paid channel groups only; compare each step with the GA4-01 benchmarks and name the worst. Checkout steps come from GA4 only; the headless visit does not go past the cart.
action: Forward the worst step and its page to the owner and developer; the Conversion review lists what is wrong on that page.
done_when: That step's rate for paid sessions is up over 14 days in GA4.
why_it_matters: Closing the worst post-click step converts more of the same paid clicks, so CVR and ROAS are expected to rise and CAC to fall.
selected_because: The core 'does paid traffic convert?' answer; the four current funnel points measure one funnel, so they merge into one paid-only point.

title: Key events count only real sales
pass: purchase is a key event, and no page_view, scroll, session_start, audience-trigger or other non-sale event is.
fails: Non-sale events are marked as key events (key events: the actions GA4 counts as conversions), so conversion rates can go above 100% and imported conversions count actions that are not sales.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-20: list_key_events; flag purchase missing, any noise or audience-trigger event marked as a key event, and key events with zero count in the period.
action: Mark purchase as a key event and unmark the rest (GA4 edit access); then check which GA4 conversions Google Ads imports.
done_when: The key events list shows only real conversions and the session key event rate is below 100%.
why_it_matters: Non-sale key events make reported conversions and ROAS read higher than real, and Google Ads bids on actions that are not sales.
selected_because: Named in the persona spec as a core over-count cause; decided by code from the key events list.

title: Tracking live with no sudden drop
pass: Events flow in realtime, and sessions and purchases show no unexplained drop week on week.
fails: No live users, or sessions fell over 40% week on week, often after a site release or GTM publish.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-15: run_realtime_report activeUsers; run_report sessions and purchase eventCount for the last 7 vs the prior 7 days.
action: Ask the developer what changed in the last GTM publish or site release and restore the tag.
done_when: Realtime shows events and the week-on-week drop is explained or gone.
why_it_matters: When tracking drops, GA4 misses sales, so reported ROAS reads lower than real and good campaigns can get cut.
selected_because: A broken tag invalidates every other number; must be ruled out before judging campaigns.

title: Payment gateways taking credit for paid sales
pass: No payment gateway (Tabby, Tamara, Tap, PayTabs, a bank 3-D Secure page) shows as a session source.
fails: Gateway domains show as referral sources with purchases, taking credit from the paid campaign that brought the buyer.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-19: run_report dimensions=[sessionSource, sessionMedium] metrics=[sessions, transactions], matched against a gateway domain list.
action: Add the gateway domains to the unwanted referrals list in the GA4 data stream (whoever has GA4 edit access).
done_when: No gateway domain appears as a source with purchases over 7 days.
why_it_matters: Sales credited to a gateway are taken from your campaigns, so paid ROAS in GA4 reads lower than real.
selected_because: Common in GCC stores using BNPL; the persona spec names it directly.

title: Paid landing pages that don't convert
pass: No landing page with real paid traffic converts under a third of the store average.
fails: A landing page that gets a large share of paid sessions converts under a third of the store average.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days dimensions=[landingPage, sessionDefaultChannelGroup] metrics=[sessions, transactions], paid channel groups only; compare each page with the store average (GA4-06 rule).
action: Send ad traffic to a page that converts, and forward this page to the developer with the Conversion review findings for it.
done_when: The page converts at half the store average or more, or no paid traffic lands on it.
why_it_matters: Paid clicks landing on a weak page are bought and lost, so CVR is low and CAC higher than it needs to be; fixing it is expected to raise ROAS.
selected_because: Page-level view across campaigns; the current point covers all traffic, the buyer needs paid only.

title: Paid sessions with an unknown source
pass: Unassigned and (not set) are under 10% of sessions, and paid traffic lands in a paid channel group.
fails: Over 10% of sessions have no known channel, or paid campaigns fall into Unassigned or Referral because of untagged links or mediums GA4 does not recognise.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-08: run_report 28 days dimensions=[sessionDefaultChannelGroup] metrics=[sessions, transactions]; list the top source/medium pairs inside Unassigned.
action: Tag every ad, bio, WhatsApp and SMS link with UTMs; for Unassigned pairs from ad platforms, change utm_medium to a value GA4 counts as paid.
done_when: Unassigned under 5% of sessions and no ad platform source sits in Unassigned.
why_it_matters: Paid sales hidden in Unassigned are not credited to your campaigns, so paid ROAS in GA4 reads lower than real.
selected_because: Unattributed sessions hide paid results; the buyer can fix most of it in their own ad URLs.

title: Session breaks between store domains
pass: The store's own domains and checkout domain never show as a session source, and links to other store domains carry the _gl linker.
fails: The store's own domain, checkout subdomain or app domain appears as a referral source, so the session restarts and the purchase loses the campaign that brought it.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days dimensions=[sessionSource, sessionMedium] metrics=[sessions, transactions], flag the store's own hostnames and checkout domains; headless visit: check whether links to other store domains get a _gl parameter.
action: Forward to the developer: set up cross-domain measurement for every store and checkout domain in the GA4 data stream, and list own domains as unwanted referrals.
done_when: No own or checkout domain shows as a source with purchases over 7 days.
why_it_matters: Each session break hands the sale to a self-referral, so paid ROAS reads lower than real and fewer purchases reach the campaign that earned them.
selected_because: Under-credit at checkout is high value for the buyer; self-referrals are readable in GA4.

title: Clean UTM names on paid links
pass: Paid source, medium and campaign values are lowercase, consistent per platform, use mediums GA4 recognises, and contain no placeholders or broken encoding.
fails: One platform appears under several spellings (Facebook, facebook, fb), mediums are invented, or values hold unresolved placeholders ({{campaign.name}}, %7B) or encoded ampersands that break the parameters after them.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days dimensions=[sessionSource, sessionMedium, sessionCampaignName] metrics=[sessions, transactions]; code flags case variants of one source, placeholder patterns ({{, }}, %7B, %7D, &), mediums outside GA4's paid list, and offline values such as utm_medium=qr that land in Unassigned.
action: Fix the URL parameters in your ad templates (Meta, Snap, TikTok, Google) to one lowercase naming scheme, and check that dynamic placeholders resolve.
done_when: Each platform shows under one source/medium pair in GA4 and no placeholder values appear for 7 days.
why_it_matters: Split or broken UTM values scatter paid sales across rows and channels, so campaign ROAS in GA4 reads lower than real and winners are harder to spot.
selected_because: The buyer owns the UTMs, so this is the one GA4 fix they can make themselves today.

title: Paid traffic on phones vs desktop
pass: For paid sessions, mobile conversion is at least 60% of desktop.
fails: Paid mobile sessions convert under 60% of paid desktop sessions, with enough visits on both.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days dimensions=[deviceCategory, sessionDefaultChannelGroup] metrics=[sessions, transactions], paid channel groups only (GA4-05 rule).
action: Forward the phone screenshots of the worst page to the developer, and fix the phone issues before scaling mobile placements.
done_when: Paid mobile conversion at 60% or more of paid desktop over 14 days.
why_it_matters: Paid clicks on phones that cannot convert raise CAC; fixing the phone page is expected to lift CVR and ROAS on mobile placements.
selected_because: Device gap on paid sessions points to a site problem, not an ad problem.

title: Paid sales from new buyers vs returning ones
pass: New-user paid sessions record purchases, and paid purchases are not almost all from returning users.
fails: Most paid purchases come from returning users while new-user paid sessions convert near zero, so paid campaigns mostly re-buy people who already know the store.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days dimensions=[newVsReturning, sessionDefaultChannelGroup] metrics=[sessions, transactions, purchaseRevenue], paid channel groups only; compare new and returning conversion and each one's share of paid purchases. Extends current fact GA4-12 (returning vs new conversion) to paid sessions.
action: If paid sales lean on returning users, split prospecting and retargeting budgets and judge prospecting on new-user sales; forward the pages new paid visitors land on to the Conversion review.
done_when: New-user paid sessions show purchases in GA4, and the new vs returning split is reviewed per campaign each month.
why_it_matters: When paid purchases come mostly from people who already buy from the store, reported ROAS reads higher than the new demand the ads create, and CAC for new customers is higher than it looks.
selected_because: Backfill: tells the buyer whether paid traffic wins new buyers or re-buys existing ones, from the store's own GA4 new vs returning data.

title: Paid sessions that look like bots
pass: No paid source, campaign or placement brings sessions with near-zero engagement and no add_to_cart, and no session spike shows without matching purchases.
fails: One paid source or placement sends many sessions with almost no engagement time and no product views, or sessions jump with no change in purchases.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days dimensions=[sessionSource, sessionMedium, sessionCampaignName] metrics=[sessions, engagementRate, userEngagementDuration, addToCarts, transactions], compare each paid row with the store's paid average; run_report dimensions=[date] for 90 days to find spikes without purchases.
action: Exclude that placement, audience network or source in the ad platform, then watch engaged sessions.
done_when: The flagged source's sessions drop, or its engagement rate matches the rest of paid traffic over 14 days.
why_it_matters: Bot or junk clicks are paid for but can never buy, so CAC is higher than it needs to be and CVR reads lower than real.
selected_because: Wasted paid clicks the buyer can act on in their own ad account, found from GA4 engagement data.

title: Google Ads linked to GA4
group_ar: الـ signal اللي الحملات بتتعلم منها
pass: Google Ads is linked to this GA4 property.
fails: No Google Ads link, so GA4 audiences and conversions cannot reach Google Ads and GA4 shows no Google Ads cost.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-21: list_google_ads_links. Whether purchase is the primary conversion in Google Ads is not verifiable from the audit: check in Google Ads.
action: Link Google Ads to GA4 (needs GA4 edit and Google Ads admin access) and import purchase as the primary conversion.
done_when: The link shows in GA4 Admin and purchase is a primary conversion in Google Ads.
why_it_matters: Without the link, Google bidding and audiences miss GA4 sales data, so Smart Bidding learns from less signal; fixing it is expected to improve ROAS over time.
selected_because: Direct signal path for Google campaigns; readable from the Admin API.

title: Funnel events all reach GA4 with sane counts
group_ar: الـ signal اللي الحملات بتتعلم منها
pass: view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout and purchase all record in GA4, and begin_checkout is in line with views of the checkout page.
fails: A funnel event is missing or far too low in GA4, or begin_checkout differs a lot from checkout page views, so a trigger is broken.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-17: run_report dimensions=[eventName] metrics=[eventCount] for the ecommerce events; plus run_report dimensions=[pagePath] metrics=[screenPageViews] for checkout pages compared with the begin_checkout count.
action: Forward to the developer: add or fix the missing event so every funnel step reaches GA4.
done_when: Every funnel step shows in GA4 with counts that match views of its page.
why_it_matters: Missing funnel events mean fewer signals and smaller retargeting audiences, so the algorithm learns slower and CAC stays higher.
selected_because: Without complete events the paid funnel cannot be measured; GA4's own counts show whether each step arrives, whatever sends it, so the container-only 'tag exists' check was merged here.

title: Attribution settings that decide paid credit
pass: The GA4 reporting attribution model is data-driven or another model the team chose on purpose, and the key event lookback windows are not shortened from GA4's defaults.
fails: The model is set to a Google-paid-channels-only last click, or lookback windows are shortened, so GA4 and the conversions Google Ads imports from it credit paid channels differently from what the team assumes.
validate: GA4 admin: get_attribution_settings; read reportingAttributionModel, acquisitionConversionEventLookbackWindow and otherConversionEventLookbackWindow; flag a Google-paid-only model or windows shorter than GA4's defaults.
action: Set the reporting attribution model and lookback windows on purpose in GA4 admin (GA4 edit access), note the change date, and compare campaign numbers only across periods with the same setting.
done_when: The model and windows are the ones the team chose, and the change date is recorded.
why_it_matters: The attribution model decides how much of each sale GA4 gives to paid channels and to imported Google Ads conversions, so an unplanned setting can move paid ROAS in GA4 with no change in the ads.
selected_because: Backfill: the one GA4 setting that directly changes paid credit; readable through the Admin API.

title: Retargeting audiences ready
group_ar: الـ signal اللي الحملات بتتعلم منها
pass: Cart-abandoner or product-viewer audiences exist and Google Ads is linked.
fails: Only GA4's default audiences exist, or there is no Google Ads link to use them in.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-14: list_audiences and list_google_ads_links.
action: Create cart-abandoner and product-viewer audiences in GA4 and share them with Google Ads.
done_when: Both audiences exist and show users in Google Ads.
why_it_matters: Without these audiences you cannot retarget people who already viewed or carted from GA4 data, so retargeting reach and ROAS are lower than they could be.
selected_because: A buyer-owned lever that is readable from the Admin API.

title: Product pages that get views but no add to cart
pass: No popular product's add-to-cart rate is far below the store average.
fails: A product page with many views adds to cart at under half the store average.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-10: run_report 28 days dimensions=[pagePath, eventName] metrics=[eventCount] for view_item and add_to_cart.
action: If you run ads to this product, forward it to the owner (price, photos, stock, size info on that page), or move spend to products that add to cart.
done_when: That product's add-to-cart rate reaches the store average, or ads no longer point to it.
why_it_matters: Paid clicks sent to a product that does not add to cart are wasted, so CAC rises; fixing the page or switching the product is expected to lift CVR.
selected_because: Tells the buyer which product to stop advertising or forward for a fix.

title: Order value vs free-shipping threshold
pass: The free-shipping threshold sits at 1.1–1.6× the average order value.
fails: No threshold found on the site, or it sits below or far above the average order value.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-11: AOV from purchaseRevenue / transactions, 28 days; threshold read from the live store pages and the cart in the headless visit.
action: Ask the owner to set free shipping at about 1.3× AOV and show it in the cart.
done_when: Threshold set at 1.2–1.5× AOV and visible in the cart.
why_it_matters: A threshold just above AOV encourages bigger baskets, so AOV and ROAS are expected to rise at the same CAC.
selected_because: An AOV lever measured against this store's own GA4 AOV, not a generic best practice.

title: Countries that get visits but never buy
pass: Countries with real traffic also produce sales.
fails: A country with a real share of sessions, often from paid channels, has zero purchases.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-09: run_report 28 days dimensions=[country, sessionDefaultChannelGroup] metrics=[sessions, transactions].
action: Exclude those countries from ad targeting, or confirm with the owner that the store ships there.
done_when: Paid sessions from those countries close to zero.
why_it_matters: Paid clicks from countries the store does not sell to cannot convert, so CAC is higher than it needs to be.
selected_because: Wasted paid clicks the buyer can stop in targeting settings.

title: Data comes only from the live store
pass: All sessions and purchases come from the store's live hostnames.
fails: Staging, preview, localhost, theme-editor or unknown hostnames send sessions or test purchases into the live property.
validate: GA4: run_report 28 days dimensions=[hostName] metrics=[sessions, transactions, purchaseRevenue]; flag any hostname that is not the store's live domain or checkout domain.
action: Forward to the developer: send test and staging traffic to a separate GA4 property, and filter unknown hostnames.
done_when: Only live store hostnames appear in GA4 over 7 days.
why_it_matters: Test orders and unknown hostnames add purchases that never happened, so reported ROAS can read higher than real.
selected_because: Catches fake purchases in the live numbers with one hostname report.

title: Internal links that overwrite the ad source
pass: No internal link on the store carries utm_ parameters.
fails: Banners, menus or home-page sliders link to the store's own pages with UTMs, which start a new session and replace the paid source.
validate: Public crawl of home, one collection, one product and the cart: list links to the store's own domain whose href has utm_source, utm_medium or utm_campaign; GA4 cross-check: sessionSource values that match those internal tags.
action: Forward to the developer or content team: remove UTMs from internal links and use GA4 events for banner clicks.
done_when: The crawl finds no internal link with UTMs.
why_it_matters: Each internal UTM click takes the sale away from your campaign, so paid ROAS in GA4 reads lower than real.
selected_because: A hidden under-credit cause that the crawl proves link by link.

title: Hours and days that convert
pass: Conversion is about even across the day and week.
fails: Some hours or weekdays convert far better than others, with enough volume to act on.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-16: run_report 28 days dimensions=[dayOfWeek, hour] metrics=[sessions, transactions].
action: Shift budget or set an ad schedule toward the hours and days that convert, where the platform allows it.
done_when: Ad schedule or budget split set to match in the ad accounts.
why_it_matters: Spend in hours that rarely convert raises CAC; moving it is expected to lower CAC on the same budget.
selected_because: A budget decision the buyer makes alone, from the store's own GA4 data.

title: Property currency and timezone match the store
pass: Property currency and timezone match the store's main market.
fails: Currency or timezone differs from the country most sessions and sales come from, so revenue shows in another currency and days do not line up with the ad platforms or the store admin.
validate: GA4 fact GA4-22: get_property (currencyCode, timeZone), compared with the top country by sessions and transactions.
action: Set the GA4 property currency and timezone to the store's market (GA4 edit access).
done_when: Property settings show the store's currency and timezone.
why_it_matters: A wrong currency or timezone makes GA4 revenue and daily numbers disagree with Ads Manager and the store admin, so GA4 ROAS checks are off.
selected_because: Revenue currency and day boundaries decide whether GA4 and the ad platforms can be compared.
